newsitem.title: DUBAI: OPEC expert says oil prices could gain strength.
newsitem.headline: OPEC expert says oil prices could gain strength.

text.p: An OPEC expert has said he believes oil prices could rise in the coming months due to the delay in implementing the oil-for-food plan for Iraq, the official Qatar News Agency (QNA) reported.
"One of the most important factors that could lead to an increase in prices is the delay of Iraq's sale of oil for food," Ibrahim Ismail, head of the Energy Department at OPEC, told QNA on Saturday.

The oil-for-food plan, on hold because of the recent crisis in northern Iraq, would have allowed Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil in order to buy much-needed supplies for its people, who have been hit with United Nations trade sanctions. The embargoes were imposed in August 1991 after Iraqi troops invaded Kuwait.
Ismail also said a cold winter and the inability of non-OPEC producers to keep up with that demand could also strengthen prices.

"If Iraq does come back (with the oil-for food plan) and there is a possibility that the North Sea production will rise by 300,000 barrels and there is no bitter cold, the price will not go down by more than a dollar a barrel," he said.
